summary.signal: Engineering AI is moving into deterministic execution-and-validation loops in MBSE and CAE rather than stopping at generated text.
Scientific agents are most credible when natural-language intent is connected to physics-based computation and experimentally or expert-validated outputs.
Manufacturing AI remains constrained by the digital thread: perceived connectivity materially exceeds cross-functional system integration.
Aerospace engineering signals emphasize qualification and multidisciplinary design rather than isolated prototypes.
Enterprise agent control is becoming separable from model orchestration, with customer-controlled sandbox execution as an explicit architecture layer.

central_signals: AI-assisted engineering is becoming an evidence-producing loop: model generation is paired with deterministic diagnostics, analyses and solver/tool execution.
Portable model semantics and explicit validation rules are emerging as prerequisites for safe cross-tool engineering automation.
Scientific AI gains practical credibility when physics-based computation is connected to experimental or expert validation.
Manufacturing AI value depends on cross-system feedback and data lineage; nominal connectivity does not imply an integrated digital thread.
Agent execution infrastructure is becoming a distinct governance layer covering runtime isolation, secrets, egress and artifact handling.
tensions_or_caveats: Ansys material is a webinar/product capability description rather than an independent performance evaluation.
Hexagon's State of Manufacturing study is vendor-commissioned, self-reported and U.S.-only.
DCS VOLARE claims are partially verified because the Curator's bounded direct fetch returned a cache miss; no extra claims were added beyond the Scout capture.
MiMo benchmark claims remain vendor-reported; Rafale AI flight-test details remain sparse and lack a located first-party technical release.
Seven candidates were suppressed as already published within the dedupe window without a material delta.

known_gaps: Two journal candidates with strong domain relevance lacked published_at in the Scout artifact and were not promoted without resolving that field.
The Rafale AI flight-test signal is supported by Reuters but lacked a first-party technical release in the bounded verification pass.
No strong fresh EDA candidate survived Scout discovery and dedupe.
Several performance figures are author/vendor-reported and must not be rewritten as independently reproduced results.

selected.title: AI-Augmented AADL in Visual Studio Code
selected.organization: Carnegie Mellon University Software Engineering Institute
factual_points: SEI demonstrates an open-source VS Code AADL workflow in which an AI coding agent edits a multi-file flight-controller architecture and receives domain-specific diagnostics.
The extension exposes instantiation plus latency, bus-load and mode-reachability analyses, keeping engineering acceptance outside the language model.

claims.text: The VS Code AADL workflow couples AI-generated model edits to syntax diagnostics, instantiation and three architecture analyses.
claims.evidence_location: Moving AADL into the Engineering Loop and Flight-Controller Example sections

claims.text: SEI explicitly states that passing diagnostics and analyses do not establish correctness of physical assumptions or approval authority.
claims.evidence_location: What Remains to be Understood section

selected.why_it_matters: AI-assisted MBSE is being framed as an evidence-producing loop rather than unconstrained model generation.
selected.practical_implication: Use deterministic validation, analysis artifacts, provenance and human sign-off as the acceptance boundary for AI-authored architecture changes.

provenance.source_title: AI-Augmented AADL in Visual Studio Code
provenance.verification_note: Primary SEI page re-checked. This is a material implementation follow-up to earlier AI-Augmented MBSE coverage because it adds a concrete VS Code/AADL flight-controller workflow and named deterministic analyses.

selected.title: Dimensional hyperreduction of nonlinear finite element models via empirical cubature with manifold-adaptive weights
factual_points: MAW-ECM allows empirical-cubature weights to vary with nonlinear-manifold coordinates instead of remaining fixed.

On two nonlinear finite-element benchmarks, the authors report more than two orders fewer sampled integration points than a standard linear reduced model and additional pruning versus fixed-weight manifold models.

claims.text: MAW-ECM makes empirical-cubature weights state dependent through nonlinear-manifold coordinates.
The authors report >2 orders reduction in sampled integration points and roughly 80% and >97% further pruning in two comparisons.
claims.evidence_location: Paper results summarized in Scout excerpt

selected.why_it_matters: Reduced-order modeling remains a practical route to making repeated nonlinear FEA evaluations cheaper without replacing the governing solver structure outright.
selected.practical_implication: Assess error over the actual design manifold and include out-of-distribution states before using hyperreduced models in optimization or digital-twin loops.

provenance.source_title: Dimensional hyperreduction of nonlinear finite element models via empirical cubature with manifold-adaptive weights
provenance.verification_note: No matching event found in the publication index; benchmark figures remain attributed to the authors.

selected.title: AutomationML as an Exchange Format for Tool-Independent Domain-Specific Modeling Language Specifications
selected.organization: AutomationML Association / Otto-von-Guericke University / FH Salzburg
factual_points: The accepted contribution proposes representing DSL concepts, constraints, validation rules, diagrams, templates and workflow information in a neutral AutomationML companion file.
The approach is demonstrated with a Product-Process-Resource DSL and targets equivalent modeling environments across heterogeneous MBSE tools.

claims.text: The proposal extends AutomationML from engineering-instance exchange toward portable DSL specifications and validation semantics.
A PPR DSL demonstrates capture of concepts, relations, constraints, diagrams, toolboxes, templates and workflows independently of one MBSE tool.

selected.why_it_matters: Agentic engineering depends on portable, machine-readable model semantics; moving constraints and validation rules with the model reduces tool-specific ambiguity.
selected.practical_implication: Preserve domain rules as executable/interpretable artifacts instead of relying on prompt context or proprietary GUI configuration.

provenance.source_title: AutomationML as an Exchange Format for Tool-Independent Domain-Specific Modeling Language Specifications
provenance.verification_note: AutomationML conference page re-checked; full contribution is not yet posted, so claims are limited to the accepted abstract.

selected.title: Agentic AI for Ansys Mechanical and MAPDL Workflows
factual_points: Ansys describes prompt-driven agent workflows for Mechanical and Mechanical APDL in graphical and non-graphical environments.
The webinar explicitly positions coding agents such as Claude Code, Codex, Cursor and Copilot as interfaces to simulation tasks and organizational engineering knowledge.

claims.text: Ansys states that modern AI agents can interface with Mechanical and Mechanical APDL to automate engineering tasks and workflow execution.
The described workflows include both graphical and non-graphical environments and named coding-agent integrations.

selected.why_it_matters: Commercial CAE is moving toward direct agent execution inside established solver workflows, closer to production engineering than generic engineering chat.
selected.practical_implication: Define allowed commands, model-state checks, solver convergence tests, output validation and approval gates before granting agents broad CAE execution rights.

provenance.source_title: Agentic AI for Ansys Mechanical and MAPDL Workflows
provenance.verification_note: Primary Ansys/Synopsys webinar page re-checked; no performance benchmark is inferred.

selected.title: Cloudflare expands support for Cursor Cloud Agents with customer-controlled Sandboxes
selected.category: AIエージェント・Coding・Sandbox Infrastructure
factual_points: Cursor retains the agent loop, inference and planning while terminal, filesystem, repository and browser actions execute in customer-controlled Cloudflare sandbox infrastructure.
The self-hosted-machine design uses outbound connectivity and keeps repositories, build caches and secrets on customer-operated infrastructure, subject to documented artifact uploads.

claims.text: Cursor hosts inference/planning while tool execution occurs in customer-controlled Cloudflare Sandboxes.
The design uses outbound connectivity and keeps repositories, build caches and secrets customer-side during self-hosted operation, while selected artifacts may be uploaded.

selected.why_it_matters: The execution boundary for agents is becoming separable from the model/orchestrator, enabling enterprises to control code, secrets and runtime environments independently.
selected.practical_implication: Treat sandbox placement, egress, artifact export and secret access as first-class architecture decisions for enterprise agents.

provenance.source_title: Cloudflare Expands Support for AI Coding Agents with Cursor Cloud Agents on Cloudflare Sandboxes
provenance.verification_note: Cloudflare primary release and implementation documentation re-checked; no matching published event found in the publication index.

selected.title: 77% of manufacturers call their operations connected. Only 40 really are.
factual_points: Hexagon's commissioned State of Manufacturing Report 2026 surveyed 511 U.S. manufacturing professionals through Dynata.

77% call operations fully or mostly connected, while 40% report connection across design, production, quality and business systems; 39% report limited feedback among design, manufacturing and quality.

claims.text: The survey covered 511 U.S. manufacturing professionals and was commissioned by Hexagon and conducted by Dynata.
77% describe operations as fully or mostly connected, versus 40% reporting cross-system connection; 39% report limited feedback among design, manufacturing and quality.

selected.why_it_matters: The report quantifies a digital-thread gap directly relevant to AI-enabled manufacturing: models and agents cannot close workflows if design, production and quality data remain weakly connected.
selected.practical_implication: Prioritize cross-system feedback loops and data lineage before treating plant AI as an optimization layer over a coherent digital thread.

provenance.source_title: 77% of manufacturers call their operations connected. Only 40 really are.
provenance.verification_note: Hexagon release re-checked; survey sponsorship and U.S.-only scope retained as caveats.

report_details.methodology: Hexagon-commissioned survey conducted by Dynata, spanning entry-level workers through C-suite respondents in U.S. manufacturing.
key_metrics: 77% describe operations as fully or mostly connected.
40% report connection across design, production, quality and business systems.
39% report limited feedback between design, manufacturing and quality teams.
More than four in 10 report catching quality problems too late.
report_details.comparison_to_previous: No directly comparable prior-wave metric was stated in the verified release.
report_details.practical_meaning: Perceived connectivity can substantially exceed end-to-end digital-thread connectivity; feedback across design, production and quality remains a practical integration gap.
caveats: Headline connectivity labels depend on respondent interpretation.

selected.title: MutexaGPT: an intuition-to-design translator for physics-based enzyme engineering
factual_points: MutexaGPT converts plain-English enzyme-engineering intent into physics-based modeling plans, high-throughput molecular simulations and ranked mutation proposals.
Two experimental case studies report a 40% hit rate with about 4× enrichment in one task and variants with up to 3.7× improved cold adaptation in another.

claims.text: MutexaGPT is an LLM-agent system that turns user intent into executable high-throughput molecular modeling workflows and ranked enzyme variants.
The paper reports a 40% hit rate with ~4-fold enrichment in one experimental case and variants with up to 3.7-fold improved cold adaptation in another.

selected.why_it_matters: This is a concrete closed loop from natural-language scientific intent through physics-based simulation to experimentally tested design candidates.
selected.practical_implication: Scientific agents should be judged on domain assumptions, simulation provenance and experimental validation, not only conversational competence.

provenance.source_title: MutexaGPT: an intuition-to-design translator for physics-based enzyme engineering
provenance.verification_note: Nature primary article re-checked, including publication date and two experimental case-study metrics.

selected.title: Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera
factual_points: Microsoft Research released RetroChimera implementation and weights and describes a hybrid ensemble of de-novo and template-grounded retrosynthesis models with learned reranking.
Microsoft reports that in a 10-target expert assessment, complete routes were accepted for 9 targets versus 2–5 for compared sub-models/baselines; this is source-reported.

claims.text: Microsoft Research released RetroChimera implementation and weights and describes validation including rare-reaction recall and transfer/fine-tuning studies.
claims.evidence_location: At a glance and release description

claims.text: Microsoft reports 9 of 10 targets with expert-accepted complete routes in its cited assessment, compared with 2–5 for compared sub-models/baselines.

selected.why_it_matters: Open implementation plus chemistry-specific evaluation makes this more reusable than a closed benchmark claim and relevant to materials as well as medicinal chemistry workflows.
selected.practical_implication: Reproduce route-quality evaluation on proprietary chemistry and measure chemist review burden before autonomous planning use.

provenance.source_title: Improving synthesis prediction of small molecules at scale with RetroChimera
provenance.verification_note: Microsoft Research primary page re-checked; evaluation figures remain explicitly source-reported.

A stated project aim is qualification of AML3D's Wire-Arc Additive Manufacturing process for aerospace tooling production; AML3D already holds AS9100D accreditation.

wildcards.category: 最新AIモデル・オープンウェイト・Agentic RL
factual_points: Xiaomi released MiMo-V2.6-Flash-RL under the MIT license with 309B total and 15B active parameters in a sparse MoE architecture.
The model card states native text/image/video/audio input, a 1M-token context and a mixed RL run spanning coding, general-agent, visual and cybersecurity tasks.

claims.text: The official model card lists an MIT license, 309B total/15B active sparse-MoE architecture and 1M-token context.
Benchmark and capability results on the model card are vendor-reported and are not independently reproduced here.

wildcards.why_it_matters: An open-weight, multimodal, long-context model explicitly trained across agentic tasks is strategically relevant, but direct engineering-workflow value still needs evidence.
wildcards.practical_implication: Test tool-use reliability, serving cost and domain adaptation on engineering workloads before treating broad benchmark coverage as production readiness.

provenance.verification_note: Official Hugging Face model card retained as primary; benchmark results remain vendor-reported.

wildcards.title: Dassault Aviation tests AI algorithms on Rafale fighter jet
factual_points: Reuters reports that Dassault Aviation flight-tested two AI algorithms on a crewed Rafale, one developed in-house and one with Thales.
Dassault said the functions are intended to support human crews and are mature enough to be considered for future Rafale upgrades; detailed test roles were not disclosed.

claims.text: Reuters reports that two AI algorithms were flight-tested on a crewed Rafale, one from Dassault Aviation and one developed with Thales.
The reported functions are intended to support human crews, but detailed algorithm roles and test metrics were not disclosed.

wildcards.why_it_matters: Flight testing on a crewed combat aircraft is a stronger maturity signal than laboratory autonomy demos, but the lack of disclosed function and metrics limits technical assessment.
wildcards.practical_implication: Track first-party disclosure on assurance, compute hardware, failure modes and human-authority boundaries before promotion beyond wildcard status.

provenance.source_title: Dassault Aviation tests AI algorithms on Rafale fighter jet
provenance.verification_note: Fresh Reuters report verified; bounded search did not locate a first-party technical release, so this remains a wildcard.

wildcards.title: AES100 engine and propulsion-manufacturing technologies recognized in 2026 aeronautics awards
factual_points: AECC reports that the AES100 civil turboshaft received the sole grand prize in the cited 2026 aeronautics science-and-technology awards.

Other recognized work spans additive manufacturing of high-temperature complex thin-wall engine parts, blade-clearance/transient-displacement measurement, turbine aero-thermal design/validation and combustor-liner cooling.

claims.text: AECC reports the AES100 civil turboshaft as the sole grand-prize recipient in the cited awards.
The announcement lists awarded work in additive manufacturing, blade-clearance measurement, turbine aero-thermal design/validation and combustor cooling.

wildcards.why_it_matters: The breadth of recognized propulsion work is a useful watch signal on China's engine-design, measurement and manufacturing stack, but an award notice provides limited technical evidence.
wildcards.practical_implication: Follow for primary papers, validation data or production qualification details before using the award itself as evidence of comparative technical performance.
